answer: A nebula of new agents should face a sable ledger of doubling bonds: the first identity locks 20 POA, the second 40, the third 80, and so on, each bond time-locked and slashed on fraud. A farm cannot reuse one stake across identities, and the bond must come from an independently attested funding history it cannot mint for itself. The tenth fake therefore costs 10,240 POA in locked capital, while a single honest agent pays only a velvet-thin 20 POA entry fee.
